memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: The LORD said to Moses and Aaron, "Speak to the Israelites and say to them: 'When any man has an unusual bodily discharge, such a discharge is unclean.'" - Lev 15:1-2 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God speaks about the body directly. No euphemism, no discomfort, no apology. He made this body, and He is not embarrassed by it.

That matters more than we might think. Many of us grew up in homes or churches where the body was never mentioned — where anything physical was slightly awkward, faintly shameful, best not discussed. And so we absorbed the idea that God is interested in souls and vaguely uncomfortable with bodies.

Scripture says the opposite from beginning to end. God formed a body from the dust and called it very good (Gen 1:31). The psalmist marvels: I praise you because I am fearfully and wonderfully made (Ps 139:14). And most astonishing of all, God took a body Himself. The Word became flesh (John 1:14) — with a digestive system, with tiredness, with a body that bled.

Paul goes further still and tells ordinary believers that their bodies are temples of the Holy Spirit (1 Cor 6:19).

So if illness, ageing, or bodily struggle makes you feel awkward before God, this chapter is a quiet comfort. He is not squeamish about you. He speaks to your body plainly, because He made it, He entered one Himself, and He intends to raise yours.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you carry unspoken shame about your body before God?
2. How does the incarnation change how you think about physical life?
3. What would it mean to bring a bodily struggle honestly to God today?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You that You made my body, took one Yourself, and are not embarrassed by me. Help me bring even the physical struggles I hide to You without shame. Amen.
